welcome.label: Welcome · shells on the cattails

parts.label: 🗂 The case question
parts.title: Shells on the Cattails
parts.body: Are the shells dead bugs, and what is the green case on the milkweed?

welcome.script:
Welcome, scientists! New week, new case, and this one starts at a pond.

[ON SCREEN: Jar 1]
Dr. Reyes found dozens of these on the cattail stems. Six legs. A split down the back. And they never move.

[ON SCREEN: Jar 2]
In the mud, her net caught something with the same shape, but this one swims!

[ON SCREEN: The green case]
And this was hanging under a milkweed leaf.

[ON SCREEN: The case question]
A volunteer wrote “dead bugs?” on the jar. Are they? Find four clues. Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie, right below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · what comes next? (Clue 1)

parts.label: 👆 How to play
parts.title: What comes next?
rows: Look at the stage in the Now box.
Drag the next stage into the empty box, or tap it.
Go all the way around the circle.

warmup.script:
(Hold up a closed fist, then slowly open it.) Something small can turn into something amazing.

[ON SCREEN: Egg]
A monarch starts as an egg this tiny, about the size of a pinhead.

[ON SCREEN: Caterpillar]
Then this hatches out. Hmm. It sure doesn’t look like a butterfly yet!

[ON SCREEN: How to play]
In the game, look at the Now box and pick what comes next. Keep going all the way around. Then list three things that change. Press Listen for Dr. Reyes’s hint.

part2.label: Part 2 · side by side (Clue 2)

parts.label: 📅 The slider
parts.title: Side by side
rows: Drag the slider to make the days go by.
Stop at each day listed under the slider.
Does each baby look like its parent?

part2.script:
Two babies, hatched on the same day.

[ON SCREEN: Monarch baby · Grasshopper baby]
One is a monarch caterpillar. The other is a baby lubber grasshopper, called a nymph. Which one already looks like a small version of its parents?

[ON SCREEN: The slider]
Drag the slider and watch them grow up side by side. Stop at each day listed under the slider and read the check marks. One of them is about to disappear into a green case. Press Listen on the walkie-talkie.

explore.label: Part 4 · alike and different (Clue 4)
explore.script:
(Hold up two different shoes.) How are these alike? How are they different? Scientists compare life cycles the same way.

[ON SCREEN: Dragonfly]
Look at this dragonfly. Do you see the brown thing right next to it? Hmm, where have we seen that before?

[ON SCREEN: Three boxes]
Pick a pair, then sort each fact into a box. When you finish the monarch and the dragonfly, you’ll have your last clue. Press Listen.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: Dead bugs?
parts.body: Pick the answer that fits all four clues.

parts.label: ✍️ Your case report
parts.title: Four places to write
rows: Copy your Gathered Answers into Canvas

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You have four clues. Crack the case at the top of this tab: dead bugs, or something else?

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Then write your case report. Two short answers, one Florida life cycle in Part C, and a CER. Want to draw your life cycle in a circle? That’s a bonus. Stuck? Press Hint under any box. Your answers save as you type. Press Listen.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “A caterpillar and a butterfly are completely different animals. They don’t even look alike.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The claim]
A classmate says a caterpillar and a butterfly are completely different animals. They don’t even look alike! Do you agree?

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Remember CER. Tap your side and two facts from today. Think about that green chrysalis. Then explain how your facts prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…” Press Listen.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🫙 Your specimen
parts.title: Dragonfly shell in a jar
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next time
parts.title: Winter at the pond
parts.body: How do Florida plants and animals depend on each other, and on the seasons?

closing.script:
Case closed! No dead bugs: just old dragonfly skins and a monarch getting ready to fly.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist and a dragonfly shell goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next time]
Next time, winter comes to the pond. Where do the dragonflies and monarchs go? Press Listen for Dr. Reyes’s last word.

part3.label: Part 3 · close the circle (Clue 3)
part3.script: Every life cycle is a circle. The first stage is already there. Drag the next one onto the glowing spot until the circle closes, then pick the kind of life cycle. Count the stages! Press Listen.

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.

vr.label: VR activity · Two insect families (separate page)

parts.label: 🫙 Ava’s jar
parts.title: What will they turn into?
parts.body: A girl named Ava found wiggly things in her pond. Help Dr. Reyes answer her.

parts.label: 🧭 Two ways
parts.title: Two ways to do it
rows: VR Field Mission: in the Tropical Rainforest, line up the insects that change completely and circle up the ones that grow up in steps.
No headset? Solve six mystery babies: guess the parent, then stamp the family.

parts.label: 🥇 The badge
parts.title: Golden Firefly badge
parts.body: Save your capture in VR to earn it.

vr.script:
Hi, scientists! (Wiggle your finger like a worm.) A girl named Ava found little wigglers like this in her pond.

[ON SCREEN: Ava’s jar]
She wants to know: what will they turn into?

[ON SCREEN: Two ways]
Pick your way at the top. With a headset, sort two insect families in the rainforest. Make the insects big and tell why each one belongs. No headset? Solve six mystery babies.

[ON SCREEN: The wigglers]
Here is the big clue: does the baby look like a small adult, or nothing like it at all?

[ON SCREEN: The badge]
Finish in VR to earn the Golden Firefly badge!

Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie, right below me.
